info.title: SuperPipeline agent work
info.description: The loop an agent drives a card with: claim, read, heartbeat, activities, and the verbs that end a run; plus the proposed checkpoint routes a coordinator service settles a run with. Every refusal is error.v1. Malformed JSON is 400 INVALID_JSON; a run verb this document does not name (`POST …/runs/{runId}/{other}`) is 404 UNKNOWN_RUN_ACTION; an unplanned failure is 500 UNEXPECTED. A run verb's lease is checked before anything else in its body: a missing or old `leaseEpoch` is 409 STALE_LEASE, another agent's run 403 NOT_RUN_OWNER.

403.description: SuperPipeline's Organization-plane entitlement check, which runs before any route (apps/api/src/routes/table.ts, `orgPlaneEntitlement`; apps/api/src/auth/org-plane-resolve.ts, `entitlementRefusal`). In Organization-plane mode a verified plane token whose `ent` does not name superpipeline is refused with the plane's own refusal, `{ "error": "product_not_enabled", "org" }` (fixtures/ecosystem-identity/token_claims.json, case product-not-enabled), not error.v1. It may answer any operation in this document. Outside that mode, and for SuperPipeline's own `spa_` credentials, it never answers.

org.description: The token's workspace, which has not enabled SuperPipeline.

post.summary: Claim the next ready card this agent may take
post.description: Malformed JSON is INVALID_JSON, a body that is not an object INVALID_BODY, and a field of the wrong type INVALID_INPUT. A caller with no agent identity is UNAUTHORIZED.

200.description: Work to do, or why there is none. An empty board is a 200 with `claimed: false`.

get.summary: Read the run this agent holds
get.description: Readable by the agent that claimed it, with or without a live lease.

get.summary: Read every run of the card this run holds

post.description: A missed heartbeat (15 minutes) is reclaimed.

post.summary: Post an activity: a thought, an action, a question or a strict decision
post.description: A strict decision replayed with the same request_id by the same agent answers with the stored response. A question parks the card in input-required (auth-required when `signal` is `auth`).

post.summary: Finish the turn, saying what kind of finish it is
post.description: `pass` (or no outcome on a stage that judges nothing) advances the card; `changes-needed` returns it with the findings; `needs-person` ends the run and parks the card on a question. When a completion reference is refused, the returned card also carries `handoff`.

post.summary: Submit a gated stage for a person's review
post.description: Ends the run and opens the stage's gate.
Ends the run and parks the card in input-required with the reason.
Retryable until the circuit breaker parks the card.

post.summary: Give the claim back without penalty
Link something the run produced from its own card
post.description: Idempotent on the card and url. An unknown provider is INVALID_INPUT.

post.summary: Link an execution export from the run that produced it
post.description: Allowed on a working run, and on one that ended completed or submitted, for its original agent and epoch.

post.summary: Verify, before acting, that the run's approval subject is still the one approved
post.description: The publisher's final lease fence: the stored bytes are returned only while the run, card, stage, subject, gate, account and expiry still agree.

200.description: The stored subject bytes and the gate that approved them

get.summary: Read a run's admitted checkpoint source
get.description: Proposed and off unless the deployment sets PROPOSED_CHECKPOINT_SOURCE; off, every call is 404 CHECKPOINT_SOURCE_DISABLED. Only the policy's reporter service may read it.

200.description: The admitted source, rejoined with the current run

post.summary: Admit a run's checkpoint source, once
post.description: Bind-once: a different source for the same run is CHECKPOINT_SOURCE_CONFLICT. Malformed JSON is INVALID_CHECKPOINT_SOURCE, by checkpoint JSON's own lexical rules.

200.description: The admission receipt; an exact replay returns the stored one

post.summary: Settle a run with its checkpoint report
post.description: Proposed and off unless the deployment sets PROPOSED_CHECKPOINT_SETTLEMENT; off, every call is 404 CHECKPOINT_SETTLEMENT_DISABLED. At most 64 KiB.

200.description: The settlement receipt; an exact replay returns the stored one

get.description: A cap-free historical read; never execution authority.

agentToken.description: An agent's credential: a `spa_` token from SuperPipeline, or an Accounts-issued access token whose subject is an agent principal. Roles are the `spa_` token's scopes: `claim` takes a card (`POST …/claims`), `run` drives a claimed card (`…/runs/*`). A token holding `claim` alone also passes `run`, so tokens minted before the split keep finishing their work. An Accounts token carries no scopes here; its authority is checked at claim time by the control pair. A missing or unknown credential is 401 UNAUTHORIZED; a scope the token lacks is 403 FORBIDDEN.

serviceToken.description: An Accounts-issued service access token, unexpired, with `checkpoints:read` or `checkpoints:submit`. Its principal must also be the stage policy's reporter (NOT_CHECKPOINT_REPORTER otherwise). A missing or expired token is 401 UNAUTHORIZED; a missing scope 403 FORBIDDEN.

Error400.description: The request is malformed or refused as given

Error402.description: The board or card budget cap was reached

Error403.description: The credential may not do this

Error404.description: Not found, or the feature is switched off

Error409.description: A conflict with the state the caller believed in

JsonValue.description: Any JSON value, stored and returned as given.

LeaseEpoch.description: The fencing epoch the claim returned. A value that is not the run's current epoch, or is missing, is refused with STALE_LEASE.

ApprovalSubjectEnvelope.description: The exact thing an approving answer approves: id and digest are compared byte for byte, never computed.

StrictDecision.description: Correlation only: the digest names the consumer's full decision envelope. Parsed strictly.

ApprovalDetail.description: What a person approving a strict decision is shown. Parsed strictly.

PosterSubject.description: A poster's harness-permission/v1 subject on a question (charter gate.v2 §3). Parsed strictly.

expires_at.description: RFC 3339 with seconds and a time zone.

QuestionOption.description: An option on an ordinary question: a bare string (its own name and title), `{name,title}`, or `{id,label}`. A `meaning` or `scope` outside the vocabulary is refused with INVALID_ELICITATION.

QuestionParameter.description: An ordinary question's `parameter`: its options, as a list or under `options`, and optionally the subject an approving answer approves. A question with a subject must say what every option means.

StrictDecisionOffer.description: A strict decision's `parameter`: exactly the canonical approve/deny options, in order, and optionally its approval detail. Options carry no meaning or scope; `always` alone requires a workspace admin.

Usage.description: Token and cost usage for one activity. Negative or non-finite numbers are refused with INVALID_USAGE.

repositories.description: Proposed. The repositories this card chose from a stage allowlist (run-checkpoint-policy.v2), sorted. Absent: the card names none. Fixed once the card's bench exists.

primaryRepository.description: Proposed. One of `repositories`: where the card's work starts. Only with `repositories`.

cardCheckpointPolicy.description: Proposed. The checkpoint policy of a stage whose cards choose their repositories from its allowlist. Never together with `checkpointPolicy`. Offered only to a claimant whose `checkpointProtocols` lists superpipeline.checkpoint-claim.v2.

order.description: The stage's place in the pipeline. Optional: SuperPipeline has never required it. Board create (POST /v1/boards needs only a string `key`) and the whole-pipeline write (PUT /v1/boards/{id}/stages needs `key` and `name`) store stages as sent, so a board whose stages were sent without `order` (by the API, the CLI or an agent composing one) has always returned them without it; boards made from SuperPipeline's templates and its web app carry it. Both writes sort stages by `order`, and a stage without one keeps its place, so `stages` is always in board order: a reader orders stages by their position in the array, never by `order`.

CheckpointClaimDiscovery.description: The pending checkpoint policy captured with the claim. Discovery only: never source admission or settlement authority.

selection.description: Proposed, claim protocol v2. Present only when the stage has `cardCheckpointPolicy`: how its allowlist was narrowed for this card. `policy` is then the narrowed checkpoint-policy.v1 and `policyDigest` its digest; the reader recomputes both from the stage policy and refuses any difference.

ClaimReason.description: Why a claim handed out nothing: the first reason the claim filter met. Open: the board adds reasons, and a reader treats one it does not know as "nothing to claim now". The reasons on 2026-11-22 are in x-treaty-known-values.

anyOf.description: Why the last attempt at this stage died, when there was one.

body.description: Markdown source; never interpreted as HTML.

ElicitationView.description: A question this run asked, with its answer once a person gives one.

anyOf.description: The answerer's `prn_…`, or null when the user has no principal.

RunContext.description: The whole agent read surface for one run: its card, stage, handoff, references, questions and comments.

ClaimRequest.description: Identity and capabilities come from the token; the body carries preferences. A dev-header caller may send capabilities.

maxConcurrency.description: A preference: never above the agent's configured ceiling.

checkpointProtocols.description: Proposed. Every checkpoint claim protocol this claimant speaks, sent beside `checkpointProtocol` (which a server that predates this field still reads; without it this field is INVALID_INPUT). A stage with `cardCheckpointPolicy` is offered only when this lists superpipeline.checkpoint-claim.v2.

signal.description: On a question, `auth` parks the card in auth-required; `select` is a strict decision's.

allOf.description: A strict decision is a persistent `select` question with a non-blank body of at most 8192 bytes, the canonical options, and no usage, action or result.

AddRunReferenceRequest.description: A link the run produced, on its own card. Provider, source type and external id are recognised from the url when omitted.

EvidenceReferenceRequest.description: An AgentPod execution export, linked from the run that produced it. Parsed strictly.

expectedAccount.description: Any JSON value, compared canonically with the subject's account.

CheckpointSource.description: The bind-once source a coordinator admits before it dispatches the pinned worker. Each field is the same as in run-checkpoint.v1. Parsed strictly, at most 64 KiB, with checkpoint JSON's lexical rules.

CheckpointClaimSnapshot.description: The stored source rejoined with the current stage policy and run.

selection.description: Proposed. The selection frozen with the claim, when the stage's cards choose; `policy` is then the narrowed policy.
